description: A composite figure of eight secondary-electron SEM micrographs of fracture surfaces, arranged in a 2×4 grid, all at the same magnification with a printed 50 μm scale bar in the lower-right corner of every panel. The figure contrasts the rapid fracture zone of four Fe-30.5Mn-8Al-1C (wt%) low-density steel conditions — ST (a,e), 550-6 (b,f), 600-6 (c,g) and 650-6 (d,h) — at two tension–tension stress amplitudes, Δσ/2 = 180 MPa in the top row (a–d) and Δσ/2 = 315 MPa in the bottom row (e–h). Panels (a–c) and (e–g) are fibrous, ductile-looking surfaces densely covered with equiaxed dimples of varying size separated by tear ridges, with occasional larger void-like depressions. Panels (d) and (h) are qualitatively different: their surfaces are much flatter and smoother, dominated by large planar facets with radial/step-like markings, with only limited dimpled regions between the facets. The figure makes one argument: ST, 550-6 and 600-6 fail by microvoid coalescence (ductile), whereas 650-6 fails with mixed dimple-plus-cleavage-facet morphology at both stress amplitudes. No numeric dimple-size or facet-size values are printed; only the 50 μm scale bar is quantitative.

observations.observation: The figure is a 2×4 grid of eight SEM fracture-surface micrographs, all labelled with a 50 μm scale bar in the lower-right corner.
Panels (a-c) and (e-g) show dimple-dominated fracture surfaces with abundant equiaxed dimples separated by tear ridges, consistent with microvoid coalescence.
Panels (d) and (h) (650-6) show a much flatter surface dominated by large planar cleavage facets, distinctly different from the other six panels.
The caption states the top row (a-d) corresponds to Δσ/2 = 180 MPa and the bottom row (e-h) to Δσ/2 = 315 MPa.
The caption identifies the samples as ST (a,e), 550-6 (b,f), 600-6 (c,g) and 650-6 (d,h).
The surfaces shown are the rapid fracture zones at the final fracture stage.
The citing text asserts that ST, 550-6 and 600-6 rapid fracture zones are predominantly dimpled, indicating a microvoid coalescence mechanism and ductile failure.
The citing text asserts that 650-6 displays mixed fracture characteristics with both dimples and cleavage faceted regions.
The citing text attributes the cleavage facets in 650-6 to reduced ductility caused primarily by extensive precipitation of intergranular κ-carbides.
No numeric dimple size, facet size or area-fraction values are printed on any panel; the only quantitative annotation is the 50 μm scale bar.
The mixed dimple-plus-cleavage morphology of 650-6 is present at both stress amplitudes (d and h), so it is not specific to a single load level.
